findings.failure_mode: missing or unreadable sensor file aborts the entire task/thread with a panic instead of returning a typed I/O error
findings.fix: return Result<Vec<Record>, io::Error> (or a domain I/O error enum) and propagate with ?

findings.failure_mode: malformed CSV field (non-numeric value) panics the caller; hostile input causes denial of service
findings.fix: use .map_err(|e| ParseError::InvalidValue { field: parts[0].clone(), raw: parts[1].clone() }) and propagate the error through the map

findings.problem: as u16 lossy cast from u32 parse result
findings.failure_mode: values in range 65536–4294967295 silently truncate to u16 range, corrupting sensor data without any indication of overflow
findings.fix: use TryInto::<u16>::try_into() or u32::try_into() and map the error to a typed Overflow error, or parse directly into u16 with parts[1].parse::<u16>()

findings.problem: Unbounded collect of split parts into Vec<String> with no domain cap
findings.failure_mode: a single line with millions of comma-separated fields triggers unbounded heap allocation, enabling OOM denial of service from hostile input
findings.fix: use line.split_once(',') to split into exactly two fields, or count fields and reject if >2 with a typed ParseError::TooManyFields

findings.problem: println!("loaded {}", parts[0]) — stdout I/O fused into data-loading function
findings.failure_mode: hidden side effect breaks pure-data semantics, makes the function不可composition (caller cannot suppress logging), and performs blocking I/O on a hot path
findings.fix: remove println entirely from the core path; if diagnostics are needed, inject a callback or return a separate tracing event from the shell layer

findings.problem: No bounds check on parsed u16/u32 value before constructing Record
findings.construct: Record { name: parts[0].clone(), value: parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() as u16 }
findings.failure_mode: Record can be constructed with any u16 value; no domain rule enforces what constitutes a valid sensor reading (e.g., 0–100 for percentage sensors)
findings.fix: Make Record::value a newtype BoundedU16 or add a smart constructor Record::new(name, value) that validates domain constraints and returns Result

findings.problem: Raw String from parts[0] passes directly into Record with no validation
findings.failure_mode: empty string, null bytes, or oversized names are accepted as valid sensor names; no domain invariants on Record name field
findings.fix: Validate non-empty and bounded length at the parse boundary, or use a newtype NonEmptyString for the name field

findings.problem: parts[0] and parts[1] — unchecked indexing into split result
findings.failure_mode: line with fewer than 2 comma-separated fields (e.g., empty line or trailing newline) panics with index out of bounds
findings.fix: Use line.split_once(',') which returns Option<(&str, &str)> and map None to a typed ParseError::MissingField

findings.problem: Function returns Vec<Record> with no Result wrapper; all errors manifest as panics
findings.failure_mode: every failure mode (IO error, parse error, out of bounds, overflow, allocation failure) collapses into a panic, making the function unsafe for hostile or untrusted input
findings.fix: Change signature to pub fn load_sensors(path: &str) -> Result<Vec<Record>, LoadError> with a typed LoadError enum covering IoError, ParseError, OverflowError

residual_risk: Static review identifies 9 BLOCKER findings: 3 forbidden constructs (unwrap x2, lossy as), 2 resource/boundary defects (unbounded collect, unchecked indexing), 1 hidden I/O (println), 1 domain modeling gap (no typed errors, no newtypes), 1 parse-boundary violation (raw String into Record), and 1 missing error taxonomy. No commands were run. The function as written will panic on any malformed input, missing file, or hostile payload. Full repair requires: (1) Result-returning signature with typed error enum, (2) split_once instead of split+collect, (3) remove println, (4) checked parse with domain validation, (5) newtype or smart constructor for Record.
